newsitem.title: USA: UK must go "green", Blair says.
newsitem.headline: UK must go "green", Blair says.

text.p: Britons must be prepared to make fundamental changes in their daily lives to help combat global warming, Prime Minister Tony Blair says in a speech to be delivered on Monday. Blair was putting the finishing touches on Sunday to the speech he will give to a United Nations environment conference in New York, called to take stock of progress made since the 1992 Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro.
Aides said Blair wanted to take a lead in reducing emissions of carbon dioxide and other so-called greenhouse gases that cause global warming.
"All of us in the United Kingdom -- businesses, consumers, individuls and governmnt -- will need to change our habits, our way of living," Blair says in the speech.
Britons will have to use more public transport, cut down on energy use and even change their eating habits, he believes.
Blair's strong words are likely to fuel speculation that finance minister Gordon Brown will include a series of "green taxes' in his maiden budget on July 2.
British officials said tax cuts on environmentally friendly goods, such as insulation products, were a possibility, but Blair ruled out new "green' taxes.
"We do not have proposals to introduce new environmental taxes," he told a news conference at the end of the Denver summit of the Group of Seven industrial nations.
Blair said Britain was taking the lead in Europe on global warming by setting a target of cutting carbon dioxide emissions by 20 percent, from 1990 levels, by 2010.
The European Union so far has only agreed to a 15 percent cut.
"Our targets will not be taken seriously by the poorer countries until the richer ones are meeting them," he says in the speech.

British officials were disappointed that the Denver summit failed to set specific targets for carbon dioxide emissions because of opposition by the United States but pleased that the meeting did agree on the need for a significant reduction.
Blair will argue in New York that world leaders must now come up with hard targets at a conference scheduled for December in Kyoto, Japan.

"We in Europe have put our cards on the table. It's time for the special pleading to stop and for others to follow suit. If we fail in Kyoto, we fail our children because it's in their lifetime the consequences will be felt," Blair says in the speech.
